derivation_notes:
Per-element band weights derived from three signals measured in 04_frequency_importance_eda.py:
  (1) 112G PAM4 industry priority (IEEE 802.3ck)
  (2) Per-band data std (Image 2: std curves diverge between Sdd11 and Sdd21 across spectrum)
  (3) Per-band deep-null density (Image 7 middle panel: Sdd11 nulls cluster in 0-28 GHz, Sdd21 nulls cluster in 42-100 GHz)
  (4) Per-band forward model MAE (Image 7 bottom panel: Sdd21 MAE peaks at 3.34 dB in 42-56 GHz)

element_type_map.Sdd11: return-loss type (i,j) in {(0,0), (1,1)}; = Sdd11 and Sdd22
element_type_map.Sdd21: insertion-loss type (i,j) in {(0,1), (1,0)}; = Sdd21 and Sdd12 (equal by reciprocity)
element_type_map.Sdc: mode-conversion type (i,j) in {(0,2),(0,3),(1,2),(1,3)} and mirrors at (2,0),(2,1),(3,0),(3,1); Scd = Sdc^T

Sdd11.rationale: std 8.45 dB (highest); 77% of all deep nulls; matching resonance haven
112G PAM4 Nyquist; 41% deep nulls; forward MAE peak (2.07 dB)
std 6.26 dB; only 12% deep nulls; forward already strong (MAE 1.29)
std 5.76 dB; 7% deep nulls; minimal Sdd11 information here
tail; std flat at 6 dB but mostly featureless for return loss

Sdd21.rationale: near-featureless: std 2.04 dB, 0.4% nulls, model already excellent (MAE 0.46)
112G PAM4 Nyquist; industry priority maintained even though Sdd21 data is still smooth here
Sdd21 information starts in earnest: std 12.86 dB, 31% deep nulls, forward MAE 2.57 dB
PEAK of Sdd21: std 19.63 dB, 58% deep nulls, worst forward MAE (3.34 dB)
beyond 112G spec BUT 83% of all Sdd21 deep nulls live here; the cVAE was failing exactly on these

Sdc.rationale: Nyquist; PRIMARY band for EMC compliance at 112G

Scc.rationale: minimal common-mode interest at this band
